title: Greeneville's Caden Baugh named Week 7 Player of the Week - NewsBreak
text:
By McKenzie Kane ,
48 minutes ago
GREENEVILLE, Tenn. (WJHL) — Greeneville High School quarterback Caden Baugh turned in a career night Friday, racking up 345 yards of total offense and five touchdowns as the Greene Devils downed the Cherokee Chiefs, 62-7.
His teammates don’t shy away from showing their support for the senior quarterback. Wide receiver Cole Smith said Baugh is the kind of leader the team can rally behind.
“Caden Baugh, he’s got us. Greatest quarterback in the nation. He’s going to lead us to a 14-1 state championship. I believe in this guy,” Smith said.
Friday’s performance may have backed up that claim. But this wasn’t just any matchup for Baugh. A few years ago, he and his family lived in Rogersville, where his father previously served as Cherokee’s head coach. Baugh said this game carried extra meaning and had been marked on his calendar since the schedule release.
“Oh yeah. It was definitely circled,” Baugh said. “I went to school there with them guys. I’m actually still close to some of them, you know, and playing against them. It’s fun. But it’s different. Whenever you can compete with some of your friends and win, that’s always good bragging rights. So, you know, that’s how I took it.”
The growth in Baugh’s game hasn’t gone unnoticed by his family. His grandfather, Kenny Holt, who also coaches on the Greeneville staff, said the progress has been remarkable.
“From the time he started here, I think he weighed 130 pounds soaking wet when he started as a freshman. He weighs over 180 pounds now. Just the dedication that boy gives in the weight room, it’s unbelievable,” Holt said.
His father, Greeneville offensive coordinator Cody Baugh, has seen that same dedication while trying to balance the role of coach and dad.
“There’s a fine line between being dad and being coach,” he said. “So, you know, I’ll try to do my best to be coach when we’re out here on this field, but as soon as we’re finished, it’s time to be dad again. He’s got his grandfather out here [helping] too. It goes by too fast.”
For his performance, Baugh was recognized as the WJHL High School Football Player of the Week, presented by Watauga Orthopaedics and Champion Chevrolet.
